name: vscode-bridge-for-claude-code
displayName: VS Code Bridge for Claude Code
description: Gives Claude Code a VS Code window's tools, and shows it what you have open.

configuration.title: VS Code Bridge for Claude Code

vscodeBridge.enabled.markdownDescription: Serve this window's tools to Claude Code. Turn it off in the settings of a workspace that should not serve them.

vscodeBridge.markdownEditor.selection.markdownDescription: Report the text selected in the Markdown Editor and in a SemanticDiff diff: to Claude Code's selection chip, through the `markdown_editor_selection` and `semantic_diff_selection` tools and in the prompt hook's note. Works only while `#vscodeBridge.enabled#` is on. After you turn this on, reload the window.

vscodeBridge.claudeCode.chatLinks.markdownDescription: Open the file links in Claude Code's chat in the editor that VS Code picks for the file, such as the Markdown Editor for `.md`. Works only while `#vscodeBridge.enabled#` is on.

vscodeBridge.autoApprove.markdownDescription: Run forwarded tools that ask for confirmation (open or navigate a browser page, run Playwright code) without the modal dialog. Works only while VS Code runs with this extension's proposed API enabled: add `"enable-proposed-api": ["klaster1.vscode-bridge-for-claude-code"]` to `argv.json` (**Preferences: Configure Runtime Arguments**) and restart. Without that, the dialog still shows.

vscodeBridge.executeCommand.allow.markdownDescription: Command IDs the `execute_command` MCP tool may run. `*` matches any run of characters, so `editor.action.*` allows every editor action. A command must match an allow entry and no deny entry. Only your user settings set it; a workspace cannot.

vscodeBridge.executeCommand.deny.markdownDescription: Command IDs the `execute_command` MCP tool must never run, with the same `*` wildcard. Deny wins over allow. Only your user settings set it; a workspace cannot.
